assessment: Many plant developmental processes are mediated by gradients of the hormone auxin. GNOM is a vesicle trafficking component (an ARF-GEF) that is presumably involved in the polar transport of PINs, auxin transporters that help to establish auxin gradients. Here, the authors challenge the model that GNOM acts at intracellular compartments by providing convincing microscopy evidence that GNOM primarily acts at the cell cortex and/or the plasma membrane and they hypothesize that GNOM might establish/maintain some other unknown polarity cue at the plasma membrane. These valuable findings open new questions in the fields of plant developmental biology and plant cell biology.
